title: Pair Commerce OS positioning with explicit store-builder language near the primary promise
template_or_page: Homepage opportunity; counted English page only, translations require localized editorial review
evidence: Fresh crawl homepage H1 is More than a store. Your Commerce OS.; plain online store wording appears deeper in the journey. Actual English query samples returned software/category pages; five primary competitor samples show product category, workflow, or price/fee distinctions. evidence/crawl.json; evidence/external/*-parsed.json; evidence/external/search-and-source-log.json
business_impact: An unfamiliar seller needs to recognize the product category and the next step. This is a clarity hypothesis; no measured ranking or conversion loss is established.
recommended_fix: Keep the Commerce OS identity and add a concise plain-language explanation near the main promise, connecting verified supported India commerce needs and truthful trial terms to pricing/setup/demo. Avoid launching duplicate keyword landing pages.
implementation_example: Candidate explanatory copy for editorial review: Build and manage your online store in India. Product/payment/trial qualifications must come from approved availability and commercial facts.
owner_role: Product marketing with SEO and frontend owner
effort: 0.5–1 working day for copy, localized review and metadata/browser verification; assumes offer decisions are settled, excludes deployment and experimentation observation.
dependencies: Available conversion baseline before claiming uplift
validation_steps: Inspect initial and rendered HTML at desktop/mobile widths in each supported language; confirm clear category/action and no conflicting promise; compare qualified signup/demo starts and relevant non-brand CTR when sufficiently observed.
success_indicator: Approved category/offer description is visible near the primary action and consistent across locales. Any CTR or conversion change remains a measured outcome, not a promised percentage.
failure_check: More clicks but fewer qualified starts, loss of brand clarity, contradictory translated promises or unsupported product availability would invalidate the proposed copy.
